facts.text: XYZMotion.py is a VXM controller driver for a Velmex XYZ stage
The module fixes port = 'COM4' and baud = 9600 and gives the serial read a maxWaitTime timeout
defaultVelocity is 2000 steps/s (the comment says the manual calls 2000 steps/second good)
One motor step is 0.0050 mm: stepsTomm = 0.0050 and mmToSteps = 1/0.0050
The constructor opens Serial(port, baud, timeout=maxWaitTime) and writes defaultVelocity to the X, Y and Z axes with setVelocity
home() calls moveToZero for X, Y and Z with a one-second sleep between them and then reads all positions
sendcmd appends a carriage return and writes the bytes; getresp reads one line and decodes it
waitReady sends 'V' and repeats until the reply is 'R'; the comment says B is busy, R is ready, J is jog/slew mode and b is jogging
getPosition asserts the axis is X, Y or Z, reads the reply as [axis, sign, seven digits], applies the sign and converts the steps to millimetres with 0.0050
getAllPositions reads X, Y and Z in sequence and converts each reply by 0.0050 mm per step; the English Y value divides by 24.4 while getPosition divides by 25.4
setVelocity asserts Speed > 0 and Speed <= 6000 and comments that the motor speed must be in range 1-6000
setVelocity builds 'E,C,S1M<speed>,R', 'E,C,S2M<speed>,R' or 'E,C,S3M<speed>,R' for X, Y or Z
moveToZero builds 'E,C,IA1M0,R', 'E,C,IA2M0,R' or 'E,C,IA3M0,R' and then waits for ready
move_mm converts millimetres to steps with mmToSteps, builds 'E,C,I1M<steps>,R', 'E,C,I2M<steps>,R' or 'E,C,I3M<steps>,R' and then waits for ready
move_in converts inches to steps with inTomm * mmToSteps and builds the same I1M/I2M/I3M command

The VXM class defines __init__, home, sendcmd, getresp, waitReady, getPosition, getAllPositions, setVelocity, moveToZero, move_mm, move_in and __del__ (which closes the port), and no stop, abort, halt or disable method
The module creates XYZ = VXM(port, baud, maxWaitTime), homes it, moves each axis and deletes it, so importing XYZMotion performs serial and motion I/O
The README says the repository has the early coding used to communicate with the VXM controller from Velmex
